children: , the processor and artificial-intelligence chip designer, fell approximately 2.5% to $508.10 Thursday, giving back part of the previous session's surge. The pullback came even as CFO Jean Hu projected that AI could expand the company's addressable market to roughly $2 trillion by 2030.

The operating engine is already accelerating. AMD's second-quarter results showed revenue jumping 50% to $11.54 billion, while data-center sales more than doubled to $6.7 billion and supplied 58% of total revenue. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 27% from 12% a year earlier, and management guided for approximately $13 billion in third-quarter sales.

But $2 trillion represents potential industry demand, not future company revenue. Even a 5% share would equal $100 billion, requiring AMD to deliver competitive chips, deepen software adoption and secure enough manufacturing capacity. The chart sharpens the valuation risk: the $508.10 share price stands 82.02% above the $279.15 GF Value, leaving investors little room for disappointment despite the enormous AI opportunity.

title: AMD Falls 2.5% After Declaring a $2 Trillion AI Prize
